hero.eyebrow: NASA Earth observation for farmers worldwide
hero.headline: Crop decisions backed by <wheat>satellite data</wheat>, anywhere on Earth
hero.subheadline: Enter any location. AgriShift AI reads NASA satellite data on rainfall, temperature and soil moisture, then ranks crops with a score you can inspect.

problem.title: What smallholders face
problem.body1: Smallholder farmers on plots between 1 and 3 acres face a common problem: choosing the right crop for the season relies on guesswork because local weather data is scarce or absent.
problem.body2: Unpredictable rainfall and sudden temperature shifts can damage sensitive crops. AgriShift AI delivers satellite observations directly so your planting decisions rest on measured facts, not forecasts.

dataSection.title: Satellite observations we read
dataSection.subtitle: Direct feeds from NASA Earth observation satellites, calibrated for your location

power.title: NASA POWER
power.desc: Supplies daily air temperature, solar radiation, and relative humidity for your coordinates.

gpm.title: NASA GPM IMERG
gpm.desc: Measures precipitation accumulation and tracks dry spells across 10-day observation windows.

smap.title: NASA SMAP Level-4
smap.desc: Calculates topsoil and root-zone soil moisture percentiles to determine irrigation need.

methodSection.title: How the advisory works
methodSection.subtitle: Four steps from field assessment to your farm plan

step1.title: Enter field details
step1.desc: Provide village location, plot size in acres, soil classification, and previous harvested crop.

step2.title: Read satellite telemetry
step2.desc: The system pulls current NASA POWER, GPM IMERG, and SMAP soil wetness measurements.

step3.title: Score eight crops out of 100
step3.desc: The transparent engine scores each crop on thermal window, water budget, soil fit, and rotation synergy.

step4.title: Receive your farm plan
step4.desc: Get a 4-week irrigation water schedule, rotation synergy advice, and active weather risk alerts.

harvest.title: Crop rotation and harvest management
harvest.subtitle: Balancing mechanisation and soil conservation for smallholder farms
harvest.mechanisationBody: Large-scale mechanised harvesters are rare among 1 to 3 acre smallholders, where custom hiring centres and cooperative equipment are emerging for post-harvest residue management.
harvest.rotationBody: Intensive potato and paddy cycles deplete soil nitrogen and micronutrients. Introducing short-duration legume breaks such as lentil or green gram restores organic carbon and reduces chemical fertiliser dependence.
harvest.stubbleBody: Managing paddy straw through shredding and in-situ mulching protects soil moisture for subsequent Rabi sowing while eliminating open field burning.

about.title: About AgriShift AI
about.subtitle: Satellite intelligence built for farmers who need it most
about.missionBody: AgriShift AI was built to put NASA satellite data in the hands of smallholder farmers everywhere. Precise crop advice should not require an agronomist visit.
about.whereBody: The project began in Hooghly, West Bengal, where farmers on 1 to 3 acre plots in villages like Singur needed seasonal crop guidance backed by data, not guesswork.
about.accuracyBody: AgriShift AI reads live satellite measurements, not forecasts. The 100-point score reflects current soil moisture, recent rainfall, and thermal conditions at your coordinates. It does not predict yield or profit. Field conditions, seed variety, and pest pressure always matter. Use it as a starting point, then consult your local extension officer.
about.dataBody: NASA POWER (temperature, solar radiation, humidity), NASA GPM IMERG (precipitation), NASA SMAP Level-4 (soil moisture). All data is public domain.
